`repo`: **Remove opencode.json from VCS**. (_Skip CI_)

`feat` (`actions`): **Add ConfirmationMessage support for destructive actions** ([#1413](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1413)):

* feat(actions): add custom confirmation messages for destructive actions

Added `ConfirmationMessage` property to `IExecutableAction` interface,
allowing actions to provide custom confirmation prompts for destructive
operations. The property flows through `ExecutableActionInfo`, `ActionService`,
and the `ActionInfo` API model.

- Added `string? ConfirmationMessage { get => null; }` default interface property
- Propagated through `ExecutableActionInfo` record and `ActionService` mapping
- Exposed in `ActionInfo` API response model
- Added virtual overrides in all 4 scoped base classes (`SeriesAction`,
  `GroupAction`, `EpisodeAction`, `VideoAction`)

WebUI can now display custom confirmation messages when present, falling
back to generic prompts when `null`. Only meaningful when
`RequiresConfirmation` is `true`.

* feat(actions): add confirmation messages to destructive actions

Added `ConfirmationMessage` overrides to all 15 actions that set
`RequiresConfirmation` to `true`, phrased as questions suitable for a
confirm/cancel prompt in clients.

* refactor(actions): apply review feedback on confirmation messages

- Switched `Description` and `RequiresConfirmation` on
  `IExecutableAction` to accessor syntax (`{ get => ...; }`)
- Switched `ConfirmationMessage` in the scoped base classes to
  expression-bodied properties
- Clarified the AniDB MyList sync is two-way
- Warned that a forced AniDB info refresh may extend an existing ban
- Dropped parentheticals from the purge-release messages

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Name the releases `--prune` drops**:

`PruneReleases` rewrote `manifest.Releases` and returned `void`, so a
release that pruned away the only record of a version's download URL and
checksum said nothing about it. It now returns the dropped entries,
newest first, and `BuildCommand` prints a version and channel per line
under a `Pruned N releases` header. Pruning itself is unchanged; the
no-op path stays silent. Bumped to 0.4.0 and covered in `Shoko.Tests`.

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Record release notes in the manifest**:

--release-notes, --release-notes-path and RELEASE_NOTES, in that order
of precedence. Both flags at once is an error, and an unreadable path
stops the build rather than quietly recording none. Notes are written
only when supplied, so a second runtime joining an existing release
does not blank them.

`fix` (`api`): **The log hub requires admin**:

It required authentication only, so any signed-in user could subscribe
to the whole log stream. OnConnectedAsync replays a backlog too, though
only the last 50 messages (SignalRTarget.MaxLogsCount), so the live feed
is the part that matters: anything the server or a plugin logs from then
on was readable by every account.

`fix` (`user`): **ChangeUserPassword checks its arguments**:

IUserService documents ArgumentNullException for both, and neither was
enforced. A null user reached a cast, and a null password reached
UpdateUserInternal, which reads null as 'not supplied' - so the call
returned success with the password unchanged.

`fix` (`user`): **Trim the input, not the entity**:

The line assigned a trimmed username onto the live user before any
validation had run, and nothing put it back when the throw below fired.
It also disagreed with itself: the uniqueness check and the assignment
after the error check both used the untrimmed value, so ' bob ' was
checked as ' bob ' and saved as ' bob ' while the entity briefly said
'bob'. Normalising updateData instead makes all three agree.

`feat` (`actions`): **Add a video scope to the action system**:

Added `ActionScope.Video`, mirroring the existing `Episode` scope end to
end, so actions can be bound to a single video.

- Added `VideoAction`, the scoped base class that fixes the scope at
  compile time and exposes the `IVideo` context to derived actions
- Added the two `IActionService.InvokeAsync` overloads for the video
  scope, with and without free-form invocation parameters
- Taught `ActionService` to infer the scope from `VideoAction` at
  registration and from `VideoLocal` at invocation, and to carry the
  `VideoLocalID` through to the queued job
- Taught `ActionExecutionJob` to resolve the scope entity from
  `VideoLocalRepository`
- Added `FileActionController`, exposing
  `POST /api/v3/File/{fileID}/Action/{actionID}`
- Updated the doc comments on `ActionScope` and `IScopedAction` that
  enumerate the scoped base classes by name

`fix` (`config`): **Send the visibility toggle's inverse condition**:

`VisibilityAttribute.InverseToggleCondition` was never emitted into
`x-uiDefinition`. The disable toggle beside it has always carried its
`inverseCondition`, and the WebUI reads both as non-optional
(`useVisibility.tsx:21` and `:40`), so a property whose visibility toggle
was declared inverted rendered as though it were not.

`feat` (`core`): **Resolve `Lazy<T>` from the container**:

Services caught in a dependency cycle broke it by injecting
`IServiceProvider`, holding a nullable backing field, and resolving on
first use with `??=`. That works but repeats at every site, hides the real
dependency from the constructor, and races — two threads can both resolve.

`LazyResolver<T>` is registered as an open generic, so any `Lazy<TService>`
is resolvable and a cyclic dependency can be declared in the constructor
like any other. `Lazy<T>` handles the thread-safety the `??=` did not.

`VideoReleaseService` is converted as the worked example; its
`IServiceProvider` existed only for this and is gone. `AnidbService` still
uses the old pattern in three places and can follow separately — it has a
long constructor and the change is mechanical but noisy.

Note this is only valid for singletons: the captured provider is whichever
resolved the consumer, so a scoped dependency pulled through a singleton
would outlive its scope. Equally true of the pattern it replaces; the
remarks say so.

`chore` (`api`): **Report the missing-password error on the password field**:

`AddModelError` named `Username` for "A new user must have a password
set.", so the message surfaced against the wrong field.

`fix` (`plugin`): **Drop a manifest already read from the same address**:

Keyed by package and source together, not by package alone. One package
appearing twice in a repository is meaningful - a stable manifest and a
dev manifest are the same package at two addresses, and the merge in
GetAvailablePackageManifests unions their releases on purpose. The same
package read twice from the same address is a repository listing an
entry twice, which duplicated every release it carried.

`fix` (`plugin`): **Verify declared dependencies at startup**:

`ScanForPlugins` parsed `PackageDependencies` and then nobody read them, so only
install and enable/disable enforced them. A Kahn pass over the winning entry per
id now ranks `LoadOrder` so dependencies register first, and clears `CanLoad` on
anything whose required dependency is absent, disabled, unloadable, out of range
or itself refused, cycles included. Both turn `internal set` (which drops
`required`) so a plugin cannot rewrite the verdict handed to it.

`refactor` (`abstractions`): **Let only the core write plugin state**:

`IsEnabled` and `IsPinned` follow `CanLoad` and `LoadOrder` to `internal set`,
now that the core is the only friend assembly that can reach them. That takes
the hand-written backing field for `UninstalledAt` with it: the setter swallowed
a null and an overwrite to defend a field plugins can no longer touch, and the
one writer already re-checks `IsInstalled` under `lock (_pluginTypes)`.

`fix` (`api`): **Stop excluding unknown-air-date episodes from missing-episodes query**:

`GetMissing()` required `AirDate != 0`, silently dropping episodes with an
unknown air date even when the anime has already finished airing. This
disagreed with `AniDB_Episode.HasAired`, which treats an unknown air date
on a finished anime as aired. Loosened the SQL to a coarse pre-filter and
added the exact `HasAired` check in C#, matching `AnimeSeriesService.UpdateStats`.

`fix` (`core`): **Refresh anime stats after a release is saved**:

`SaveReleaseForVideo` never triggered a stats recalculation for the anime
a file was just linked to. `AnimeSeries.MissingEpisodeCount` (and other
cached stats) only refreshed via AniDB MyList sync, group-status refresh,
or a manual API call — never via the normal file-import pipeline. This let
the dashboard's missing-episode count go stale as soon as a previously
missing episode's file was imported, disagreeing with the live
`MissingEpisodes/Series` query. Enqueues `RefreshAnimeStatsJob` for each
affected anime after a release is saved, same job used by
`GetAniDBReleaseGroupStatusJob`.

`fix` (`api`): **Serialize AniDB status update type as a string**:

UpdateType in AniDBStatusUpdateSignalRModel was serialized as an
integer by SignalR because it lacked a string enum converter, unlike the
v3 API models. Added a StringEnumConverter attribute so the
udp.stateUpdate and http.stateUpdate events match the v3 convention.

`feat` (`api`): **Move release group endpoints into ReleaseInfo with source filtering** ([#1410](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1410)):

* feat(api): move release group endpoints into ReleaseInfo with source filtering

Moved the AniDB release group endpoints into `ReleaseInfoController` and
generalized them so they are no longer hardcoded to AniDB groups.

- Added `GET /api/v3/ReleaseInfo/ReleaseGroup` — lists release groups using
  the existing `includeMissing` filter plus a new comma-delimited `source`
  filter that defaults to all sources.
- Added `GET /api/v3/ReleaseInfo/ReleaseGroup/{source}/{groupID}` — returns a
  single release group by source and ID.
- Marked `GET /api/v3/AniDB/ReleaseGroup` and
  `GET /api/v3/AniDB/ReleaseGroup/{groupID}` as obsolete.
- Parameterized the release group queries in `StoredReleaseInfoRepository`
  (`GetReleaseGroups`, `GetUsedReleaseGroups`, `GetUnusedReleaseGroups`) with
  an optional source filter, consolidating the AniDB-only bodies into a shared
  core.
- Updated `ExpressionDiscovery` and the v1 `ReleaseGroups` endpoint to return
  used release groups from all sources instead of only AniDB.

* fix(api): keep the v1 ReleaseGroups endpoint limited to AniDB groups

Reverted the v1 `ReleaseGroups` endpoint to return only AniDB used release
groups. Only `ExpressionDiscovery` now includes groups from all sources.

`fix` (`actions`): **Let a scoped action's metadata reach the interface**:

`Description`, `Category`, `RequiresConfirmation` and `Validate` are
default interface members that `SeriesAction`, `GroupAction` and
`EpisodeAction` never declared, so a derived action's own copies were
unrelated members and nothing read them. All 17 series actions reported
`Miscellaneous`, no description and no confirmation. The base classes
declare the four `virtual`; 45 derived members gain `override`.

The Plex response models are pure deserialization bags, so their properties

and the `SVR_*` wrappers got honest annotations on their private surface.

- Applied `= null!` across `Shoko.Server/Plex/Models` and the `PlexEvent` bag in `PlexWebhook`
- Made `GetEpisode`, `Scrobble` and `GetShowsForDirectory` honest about nullable results
- Matched the annotated Newtonsoft base signatures in `PlexConverter`
- Adapted to `RepoFactory` getters now returning nullable values

`chore` (`api`): **Silence nullable warnings across APIv1, APIv2 and legacy filters**:

These are frozen legacy surfaces, so suppression was preferred over honest
annotations wherever an honest signature would have rippled into callers.

- Applied `= null!` to the v2 response DTOs and the legacy `Playlist`/`Scan` models
- Kept `LegacyMappings` and `LegacyConditionConverter` returning `null!` on their `suppressErrors` paths
- Made a few genuinely-optional v2 declarations and optional parameters nullable
- Aligned the `CompareTo` and `Equals` overrides with their nullable base signatures

`chore` (`db`): **Annotate nullability across the database layer**:

No migration logic was changed. `DatabaseFixes` only gained annotations and
null-forgiving operators, so existing failure modes are preserved exactly.

- Matched the annotated `TypeConverter` and `IUserType` base signatures in `Databases/NHIbernate`, widening `NullSafeGet` to return `object?`
- Changed the shared `Tuple<bool, string>` result to `Tuple<bool, string?>`, since the error message is null on success
- Made the mutually-exclusive `Command`, `UpdateCommand` and `DatabaseFix` members of `DatabaseCommand` nullable
- Applied `= null!` to the raw-SQL `DNF_*` and `DBF_*` row bags

`chore` (`db`): **Annotate nullability across the repository layer**:

Repository getters that can legitimately miss now return nullable values,
which is the root of most of the nullable annotations elsewhere in this series.

- Applied `= null!` to the 69 `RepoFactory` static fields, all of which are assigned in its constructor
- Made `IRepository.GetByID` and the `BaseCachedRepository`/`BaseDirectRepository` overloads return `T?`
- Added `where S : notnull` to the repository generics and `where T : notnull` to `ChangeTracker`
- Made the repository callback properties nullable, matching their `IRepository` declarations

`chore` (`anidb`): **Annotate nullability across the AniDB providers**:

Parser-filled response models use `= null!`, while fields AniDB genuinely
omits were made honestly nullable.

- Made the `HttpAnimeParser`, `RequestVotes` and `AniDBTitleHelper` lookups return nullable values
- Annotated `UnescapeXml` with `[return: NotNullIfNotNull]`, which removed six downstream warnings
- Made `ResponseResource.ResourceID`, `ResponseCharacter.CharacterKanjiName` and `ResponseLogin.ImageServer` nullable

`chore` (`api`): **Annotate nullability across APIv3 and SignalR**:

APIv3 is the current API surface, so these are honest annotations rather than
suppressions. Adding `?` to a response DTO changes only the C# annotation, not
the emitted JSON.

- Changed `object sender` to `object? sender` on the 18 SignalR event handlers
- Made the `FilterFactory` expression-tree and sorting-criteria signatures honestly nullable
- Made the optional controller parameters (`includeDataFrom`, `search`, `childItems`) nullable
- Added the missing `<param>` tags and fixed the malformed and ambiguous doc references

`chore` (`core`): **Annotate nullability across MediaInfo and utilities**:

MediaInfo genuinely omits tracks and fields for many files, so `MediaContainer`
got honest `?` annotations throughout. The MessagePack layout is unchanged: no
`[Key]` index, `[Union]` index, or serialized member was added, removed,
renamed, retyped or reordered, so stored `VideoLocal.MediaInfo` blobs still
deserialize.

- Made the `Stream`, `VideoStream`, `AudioStream`, `TextStream` and `MenuStream` members honestly nullable
- Bridged the non-nullable `IMediaInfo`, `IVideoStream` and `IAudioStream` members with explicit implementations
- Matched the BCL signature on the `AsyncObservableCollection` event handlers

`chore` (`core`): **Annotate nullability across scheduling, services and tasks**:

No concurrency attribute, acquisition filter or scheduling semantic was
changed.

- Marked the always-supplied job inputs `required`, e.g. `AddFileToMyListJob.Hash` and `HashFileJob.FilePath`
- Applied `= null!` where a value is assigned by `PostInit` or a constructor switch the compiler cannot follow
- Added `[NotNullWhen(true)]` to the `AutoAnimeGroupCalculator.BuildGroupGraph` out parameters
- Absorbed the nullable `RepoFactory` getters in `AnimeSeries.AnimeGroup` and `VideoLocal_User.User`

`chore` (`tests`): **Enable nullable in `Shoko.Tests` and clear the xUnit analyzer warnings**:

`Shoko.Tests` was the only project missed by the earlier solution-wide nullable
enablement, which is what produced its `CS8632` warnings. Enabling it surfaced
66 further warnings that were previously invisible; those are fixed here too.
No test was weakened, skipped, deleted, or had its assertions changed.

- Added `<Nullable>enable</Nullable>` to `Shoko.Tests.csproj`
- Passed `TestContext.Current.CancellationToken` at the 115 `xUnit1051` call sites
- Replaced `Assert.Equal(1, x.Count)` with `Assert.Single` and an `Assert.Empty` negation with `Assert.DoesNotContain`
- Applied `= null!` to the `TestFilterable` and `TestServerSettings` doubles

`repo`: **Treat compiler warnings as errors**:

The solution builds clean in `Debug`, `Release`, `ApiLogging` and `Benchmarks`,
so lock that in before it can regress.

NuGet audit advisories are excluded, since they are published out-of-band and
would otherwise break the build with no change on our side.

`fix` (`abstractions`): **Make the optional media stream members nullable**:

`IVideoStream.Resolution`, `FrameRateMode`, `ScanType`, `ColorSpace` and
`ChromaSubsampling`, plus `IAudioStream.ChannelLayout` and `CompressionMode`,
were declared non-nullable but are null for many files. `CL_Media` already
null-conditionals four of them, and `GetStandardResolution` returns `string?`,
so the contract was misleading plugin authors into unguarded dereferences.

This matches the nullability already declared on the neighbouring
`IVideoStream.MatrixCoefficients` and `IAudioStream.BitRateMode`.

- Dropped the `!` bridges in `VideoStream` and `AudioStream`, so the backing properties now implement the members directly
- Made the matching `MediaInfo` APIv3 response properties nullable; the emitted JSON is unchanged

`fix` (`db`): **Use the WebAOM provider ID for migrated `GroupAwareRenamer` scripts**:

The `GroupAwareRenamer` branch sits inside `if (providerInfo is null)` but read
`providerInfo.ID`, so migrating any legacy `RenameScript` with that renamer type
threw a `NullReferenceException`. The surrounding code already builds the
configuration from `webAomRenamer`, which is the intended provider.

`fix` (`buildtools`): **Guard `ExtractGetV5TypeName` against a missing argument list**:

`inv.ArgumentList?.Arguments.Count < 1` lifts to a `null < 1` comparison that
evaluates to `false`, so a null argument list skipped the `continue` and was
dereferenced on the next line. Replaced with a property pattern that fails to
match on null.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Stop adding nulls to the parsed staff and character lists**:

`ParseStaff` and `ParseCharacter` return null when the `id` attribute is not an
int, but `ParseStaffs` and `ParseCharacters` added the result unchecked, so a
null reached `AnimeCreator`. Both now skip nulls, matching `ParseTags`.

`UnescapeXml` also never recursed: it decoded the original argument on every
iteration instead of the previous result, so the second pass always equalled the
first and the loop returned after decoding exactly once. It now feeds each
round back in, which is what the surrounding comment describes.

`fix` (`plex`): **Return `BadRequest` for an unknown user in `SyncForUser`**:

`RepoFactory.JMMUser.GetByID` can miss, and the result was dereferenced before
the `BadRequest("Invalid User ID")` below could be reached, so an unknown user
ID produced a `NullReferenceException` instead. Also constrained `userID` to a
positive range.

`fix` (`api`): **Emit the value of a bool filter parameter instead of its type name**:

`IWithBoolParameter` called `ToString()` on the expression object rather than on
`Parameter`, so `/api/v3/Filter` reported a lowercased type name in place of
`true`/`false`. Every other case in the switch reads `Parameter`.

`fix` (`anidb`): **Avoid dereferencing a missing vote in `SyncAniDBVotesJob`**:

The guard above only skips when the vote is absent *and* the user has no rating,
so a user-rated series with no AniDB vote reached the `VoteType` read with a
null vote. A property pattern keeps the temporary-vote fallback without the
dereference.

`chore` (`abstractions`): **Bump abstractions version to v6.0.0-alpha.78**.

`feat` (`buildtools`): **Add --tag, and stop dropping the revision**:

The version was truncated to three parts when read back off the
assembly, so a four-part dev version never reached the manifest and the
Dev-channel inference on it could never fire. The tag was inferred by a
describe that only matches `v*`, so a repo tagging `<name>-v1.2.3` got
`v1.2.3` recorded instead; --tag now overrides, inference is the
fallback, and the tag reaches the manifest entry rather than stopping
at the assembly stamp.

`fix` (`workflows`): **Fetch tags on checkout and don't error on existing publish tags**:

Tag detection failed because actions/checkout only fetches a shallow
snapshot of the pinned SHA and skips tags unless fetch-tags is set, so
version stamping via git describe found no tags in the clone.

- Added fetch-tags: true to every checkout step in the daily and release
  builds
- Replaced the invalid force_push_tag input on rickstaa/action-create-tag
  with tag_exists_error: false so re-publishing doesn't fail when the
  release tag already exists

`feat`: **Add plugin-registrable action system (RFC #1380)** ([#1404](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1404)):

* feat(abstractions): add plugin-registrable action system

Implemented the RFC from discussion #1380 (v7): plugins and core can now register discrete, invokable actions that are listed through the API, filtered by scope and caller permission, and always executed through the job queue.

- Added `IExecutableAction` with a required `Name`/`Permission`, an optional `Validate` pre-check, a `RequiresConfirmation` UI hint, and `SeriesAction`/`GroupAction`/`EpisodeAction` base classes with an internal `IScopedAction` context setter, plus `IActionCaller` for caller identity.
- Added the `ActionService` registry with load-time validation, UUIDv5 action IDs namespaced by plugin ID, and `ActionExecutionJob` as the single queue-backed execution wrapper.
- Added the listing and invoke endpoints: `GET /api/v3/Action?scope=`, `POST /api/v3/Action/{actionId}`, and `POST /api/v3/{Group|Series|Episode}/{id}/Action/{actionId}`.
- Ported 60 existing actions from `ActionController` and the scoped controllers to the new shape, including bucket-1 variant pairs and bucket-2 open-ended property sets; the legacy endpoints remain available but are marked obsolete.
- Registered core actions transient in DI and plugin actions via `PluginManager`; added `InternalsVisibleTo` to `Shoko.Abstractions` so the load-time `IScopedAction` guard is enforceable.

* feat(abstractions): expose action listing and invocation to plugins

Added the plugin-facing contract so plugins can enumerate registered actions and invoke them programmatically, not just through the HTTP API.

- Added `IActionService` to `Shoko.Abstractions` with `GetActions`/`GetActionInfo` listing and typed `InvokeAsync` overloads for global, series, group, and episode scopes.
- Moved `ExecutableActionInfo` into `Shoko.Abstractions` without the concrete action type so the plugin-facing surface never leaks server internals; the server keeps the type in a private registry entry.
- Invocations now validate that the action's scope matches the supplied entity, require a caller for `IActionCaller` actions, and skip the permission gate for trusted programmatic calls without a caller.
- Dropped the separate core action registrations (the DI sweep in `SystemService` and the extra core `AddParts` call in `PluginManager`): the plugin manager already discovers core action types, since the core is registered as a plugin like any other.

* docs(actions): fix unresolved XML doc references

Replaced a `<paramref>` on a type-level remark and an unresolvable `ActionService` cref with plain text, so `Shoko.Abstractions` builds with zero warnings.

* fix(actions): harden caller resolution and category name fallback

`ActionExecutionJob` now only resolves the calling user when a caller was recorded, so trusted programmatic invocations never fail with a missing-user error. `ActionService.AddParts` marks the assembly-name fallback for `PluginInferred` categories as non-null.

* feat(actions): support bucket-2 invocation parameters

`IActionService.InvokeAsync` gained parameter-accepting overloads for all four scopes, `ActionExecutionJob` carries a `Parameters` payload through `JobDataJson`, and the job populates the matching public settable properties of the action instance before executing — the Gap 23 bucket-2 mechanism for programmatic invocation.

* fix(actions): return 404 for unknown action IDs on scoped routes

The series/group/episode invoke routes now check for an unregistered action ID and return a clean 404, matching the global route instead of surfacing an unhandled `KeyNotFoundException`.

* fix(actions): include parameters in dedup key and validate against them

Made `Parameters` a `[JobKeyMember]`, so invoking the same action on the same scope and caller with different parameters enqueues instead of silently collapsing into an already-queued job. Also moved parameter population into a shared helper and applied it to the probe instance before `Validate()`, so validation observes the caller-supplied values rather than compiled-in defaults.

* docs(actions): reword planning and migration-scoped comments

Dropped the "Gap N" planning-doc references and the "matches today" temporal parity notes left in code, per review. The surrounding prose was kept and reworded to state the what/why directly: permission comments now describe the legacy endpoints admin gate as a permanent invariant, and the execution comments describe the transient lifetime, queue-only execution, and bare-ack contract without the numbered spec tokens. Also fixed the stale `IScopedAction` guard framing and a missing word in `IExecutableAction` docs.

* chore(actions): remove legacy parity comments from action permissions

Removed the per-action comments noting whether the legacy endpoint was
admin-gated. The `ActionPermission` value is self-documenting and the
migration parity rationale does not belong in the shipped code.

`repo` (`workflows`): **Replace archived publish-nuget action, resolve Node 20 deprecation** ([#1401](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1401)):

brandedoutcast/publish-nuget is archived (unmaintained since 2022) and its
Node 20 runtime is being force-run on Node 24 by GitHub's runners, surfacing
a deprecation warning on every build. Replaced it in build-daily.yml and
build-release.yml with a composite `./.github/actions/publish-nuget` action
that wraps `dotnet pack`/`dotnet nuget push --skip-duplicate` plus the
existing `rickstaa/action-create-tag` step to preserve tag-on-publish
behavior. Also bumped `build-daily.yml`'s explicitly pinned `node-version: 20`
(used for the release-info npm packages) to 24.

`fix` (`tmdb`): **Add season-scoped nearest-air-date fallback for episode linking** ([#1389](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1389)):

* fix(tmdb): add season-scoped nearest-air-date fallback for episode linking

`TryFindAnidbAndTmdbMatch` previously fell straight from the strict
±2-day `TryAirDateMatch` window to a blind positional `FirstAvailable`
guess, which mismatched delayed/compressed episodes onto the wrong
TMDB slot (e.g. AniDB episode 2 grabbing episode 5's TMDB entry).

- Added `TryNearestAirDateMatch`, tagged with a new
  `MatchRating.NearestDateMatches` (distinct from the strict-window
  `DateMatches`), using the unbounded `CalculateAirDateDistance` to
  pick the closest remaining candidate by air date instead of by list
  position, bounded by `MaxFallbackDifferenceInDays` (120) so it can't
  confidently link episodes separated by an unrelated multi-month gap.
- Scoped the fallback candidate pool to `anchorSeasonNumber`, resolved
  from whichever neighboring AniDB episode already has a confirmed
  TMDB link (via an incrementally maintained `Ordering == 0` primary-
  link dictionary, not a linear scan), so a back-to-back multi-cour
  release (e.g. season 1 ending in March, season 2 starting in June)
  can't have this pull an unresolved episode across the season
  boundary. When neighbors disagree on season, the closer one by air
  date wins instead of always preferring the previous episode.
- `ResolveRankedMatch`'s cache-reuse now also invalidates when a
  same-pass neighbor resolves a new anchor mid-pass, not just when the
  cached TMDB candidate gets claimed.
- `CalculateAirDateProbability` now delegates to
  `CalculateAirDateDistance` instead of duplicating the day-diff math.

`fix` (`workflows`): **Don't fail nuget publish when release tag already exists** ([#1405](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1405)):

The daily build republishes packages whose version wasn't bumped since
the last successful run. dotnet nuget push --skip-duplicate already
tolerates this for the package itself, but rickstaa/action-create-tag
was still hard-failing every Publish *Nuget job on reruns because the
git tag from the prior publish already exists.

`fix` (`workflows`): **Force-push the release tag on nuget publish** ([#1406](https://github.com/ShokoAnime/ShokoServer/pull/1406)):

#1405's tag_exists_error: false never took effect: action-create-tag's
existence check is git tag -l, a local check, but the daily-build
runner does a fresh checkout with no tags fetched — it always sees
'not exists' locally and tries to create+push the tag fresh, which the
remote then rejects since the tag is already there. force_push_tag
force-pushes unconditionally, which is a no-op when the tag already
points at the same commit.

clients can fetch a deduplicated, paginated list of images for a single
image type instead of the cross-reference endpoint, which returns duplicate
rows when an image is both linked and pinned as the default.

Relocated the default-image endpoints to a `/Default` suffix to free up the

`fix` (`db`): **Add missing primary keys on SQL Server for 38 tables**:

SQLite and MySQL both declare PRIMARY KEY on these tables' identity
columns; the SQL Server migration file never did, leaving them as
heaps. Confirmed live via sys.dm_db_missing_index_details on a
production instance — TMDB_Episode_Cast and TMDB_Episode alone
accounted for the two highest-impact missing-index findings, forcing
RID lookups instead of clustered-key seeks on every query.

Adds migration 180: ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT PRIMARY KEY
CLUSTERED for all 38 affected tables. Dry-run tested in a rolled-back
transaction against a live production database with no conflicts.

Wrapped every async void event handler in the aggregate hub emitters in
try/catch so exceptions can no longer escape into the threadpool as
unhandled exceptions and crash the server. Made the file deleted event
tolerate unresolvable managed folders.
